Dutch AI. Close by. Sovereign.

We take care of your AI solution from consultation to installation, including the necessary hardware or server environment. With local AI, your data remains under your own control, without any external token costs.

About AITJE

## Who we are

Always nearby. Always available. Entirely in-house. With local AI solutions, you remain independent of the internet, external providers and platform failures. Your data stays within your organisation and you avoid unnecessary subscription costs.

We help you use AI more intelligently, more securely and more cost-effectively: with clear products, expansion options and personalised support.

The power of AI, without relinquishing control.

02 / In control

## Your own AI. A world full of possibilities.

Your knowledge is valuable. So are your tools. AITJE helps you use AI in an environment that you remain in control of.

On your own hardware or server where appropriate. Using external models where they add value. The task determines the solution.

A Dutch AI product company and specialist. Proprietary products, up-to-date knowledge and staff who remain accessible.

Dependence should be a conscious choice, not an unintended consequence. That is why AITJE brings knowledge, models and technology closer to your work.

AI is becoming indispensable. But who are you dependent on? Your team relies on it, your processes run on it, and more and more business knowledge is being fed into it. What happens if the provider raises its prices, changes the terms and conditions or goes offline for a day?

AITJE is a Dutch AI specialist in local AI, automation and smarter workflows. Proprietary AI products, consultancy, development, installation and support, with independence as our guiding principle.

- [AITJE Assistent: Your own AI chat assistant. Under your control.](https://aitje.com/en/products/aitje-assistent): AITJE Assistent: local chat with knowledge base. Stand-alone product €499; from €599 including basic installation. Excl. VAT and infrastructure.
- [AITJE Coder: Your own coding agents. With no external token costs.](https://aitje.com/en/products/aitje-coder): AITJE Coder: your own local coding agents. Stand-alone product €699; from €799 including basic installation. Excluding VAT and infrastructure.

## Prices and conditions

Hourly rate: €75. All prices exclude VAT.

AITJE Assistent: €499 (self-installation); €599 (with basic installation; regularly from €698). Introductory offer for Assistant and Coder for the first 100 paying customers. Availability will be confirmed in your quotation.

AITJE Coder: €699 (self-installation); €799 (with basic installation; regularly from €898). Introductory offer for Assistant and Coder for the first 100 paying customers. Availability will be confirmed in your quotation.

AI-scan: €395 (regular €495). Introductory offer for the AI-scan for the first 10 paying customers. Availability will be confirmed in your quotation.

Hardware, server rental, travel or on-site costs and additional configuration are quoted separately.

- [AI-scan: Where can AI improve your work?](https://aitje.com/en/services/ai-scan): AITJE’s AI-scan: approximately four hours of analysis covering up to three processes, a concise report and a discussion. Introductory price: €395, excluding VAT.

Lower costs per result.](https://aitje.com/en/services/token-management-en-optimalisatie): AITJE Maps out AI usage and costs for content, knowledge, images and code. Optimise subscriptions, models and workflows. Available as a standalone service or as a follow-up to the AI scan.
- [Advice and analysis: Got an AI question? Take the next concrete step.](https://aitje.com/en/services/advies-en-analyse): From AI enquiry to a workable plan. ‘AITJE’ examines architecture, models, costs, test cases and guardrails. Fixed hourly rate and hours agreed in advance.

Delivered ready for use.](https://aitje.com/en/services/installatie-en-inrichting): AITJE selects and configures hardware, a server or GPU-VPS for your AI solution. This can also be done on existing hardware or your own hosting. Software, models and storage are ready to use.

- [Safe use of AI: Greater control over your AI and your data.](https://aitje.com/en/services/veilig-ai-gebruik): AITJE Helps limit AI usage through anonymisation, role-based access rights for RAG, guardrails, human oversight and budget limits. Insight into data locations and retention policies.
- [AITJE Custom — Bespoke AI: Everything to do with AI. Tailored to your work.](https://aitje.com/en/services/aitje-custom): Bespoke AI: workflows using n8n or Zapier, bespoke apps, agents and 3D/VR. AITJE helps you choose and build, with local or external AI and control over data and costs.
- [Support and maintenance: Help today. Thinking ahead to tomorrow.](https://aitje.com/en/services/ondersteuning-en-onderhoud): AITJE continues to support you through Core, Plus or Max. Included are service hours, models, prompts, skills, AI health check advice, and relevant analyses and workflow demonstrations.

# AI specialist for IT companies and agencies

Official page: https://aitje.com/en/services/voor-it-bedrijven

> Your clients are asking for AI. AITJE helps IT companies and agencies with the research, development and management of AI solutions. You maintain the client relationship and stay in control.

AITJE is a Dutch AI specialist in local AI, automation and smarter workflows. Proprietary AI products, consultancy, development, installation and support, with independence as our guiding principle.

How ‘AITJE’ can help

## An AI enquiry from your client. What now?

Whether you manage servers, build websites or develop apps, AITJE adds specialist AI expertise and implementation to your service offering.

The division of roles

## You’re in control. AITJE helps build.

AITJE operates as a technical subcontractor within your project. First, the AI component, the price and the responsibilities are agreed. You can then present a clear proposal to your client.

The exact tasks and lines of communication are agreed upon for each assignment.

This is how an assignment might proceed

## “Can visitors ask questions about our products?”

A web agency manages a client’s website. That client wants to provide visitors with immediate answers based on product information and documents. The agency manages the website; AITJE builds the AI functionality.

Prepares the quotation, handles customer communications and determines how the feature fits into the website.

Assesses the sources, selects the AI configuration and builds the agreed integration.

Example of a potential collaboration.

Technical collaboration

## AI that fits into the existing environment.

Your client’s website, server or app is the starting point. AITJE examines systems, data and management before selecting a model or infrastructure.

Your own equipment, a server or an external service, whichever is best suited to the project.

Integration with the website, app, knowledge base or existing business software.

Discuss which data is processed where and who needs access.

Tailor the choice of model and workflow to quality, usage and cost per result.

From client enquiry to delivery

## Clarity first. Then your quote.

AITJE Define the technical AI aspects before you present them to your client. The amount of research required depends on the specific requirements.

Have you already received an AI enquiry from a client? The solution doesn’t have to be finalised just yet.

At the client’s premises

## You decide how AITJE fits in.

Whether working behind the scenes or in consultation: for each assignment, you agree who will approach the client on whose behalf.

Standard ‘AITJE’ products retain their names. Bespoke solutions can be delivered under your name where appropriate.

Upon completion

## The client will ring you. You can refer to AITJE for further information.

Day-to-day enquiries are handled by your company. In the event of faults, model changes or upgrades, AITJE will assist with the agreed AI-related aspects.

Set out in advance who is available to deal with what. That way, your customer will know who to contact.

# Case studies

Official page: https://aitje.com/en/cases

> AI in day-to-day work: searching through internal knowledge, linking work processes and developing software. Explore the applications and approach of AITJE.

AITJE is a Dutch AI specialist in local AI, automation and smarter workflows. Proprietary AI products, consultancy, development, installation and support, with independence as our guiding principle.

- [Ten models. One team. Control and independence.](https://aitje.com/en/cases/chatgpt-of-codex-in-je-eigen-organisatie): AITJE set up a shared AI environment for a development agency, featuring Assistent, Coder and ten models to choose from. A shared token pool of €350 per month replaces nine subscriptions to €200. Model usage and token costs per task can be tracked via Asana.
- [350 clients. One central workspace.](https://aitje.com/en/cases/council-hub): Following a takeover, a marketing company’s client base grew from 150 to 350. AITJE brought together client data, tickets, projects, invoicing information and call transcripts in a central hub. Staff can search for and chat with their business experts, with access based on their role and AI integrated into an existing Mac mini.
- [25 New game levels every week. With no external token costs.](https://aitje.com/en/cases/coder-game-in-24-uur): A marketing agency took over an existing mobile puzzle game but ran into difficulties when creating new levels. AITJE analysed the game, built a reusable level design system and linked AITJE Coder to Qwen on its own server. Now, the agency 25 creates new levels every week from a single assignment in OpenCode.
- [From technical drawing to 3D product model.](https://aitje.com/en/cases/3d-productmodellen-met-ai): AITJE built a workflow for a partner specialising in contact cables that converts product data and technical drawings from WordPress into 3D models. AITJE Coder controls Blender; Three.js makes the GLB files usable on the website. Following optimisation, API costs fell from approximately €9 to €0.11–€0.18 per product.
- [Your firm’s expertise. An assistant that works with it.](https://aitje.com/en/cases/documenten-doorzoeken-en-lakken): For an estate agency, AITJE linked Realworks, email inboxes and Google Drive to its own AI assistant. Staff chat with the knowledge relevant to their role. The website chatbot uses a separate, carefully selected knowledge base from the same environment.
- [Hey Bob. An extra pair of hands in the workshop.](https://aitje.com/en/cases/spraak-naar-werkorder): AITJE, developed a voice-controlled application for a local garage that serves over a hundred customers a day. Six Android tablets connect mechanics to technical information, work orders and their administrative records – simply by asking.
- [6,900 Products enriched and translated in 7 hours](https://aitje.com/en/cases/productteksten-zonder-tokenkosten): AITJE built a workflow for a leading Dutch online shop specialising in chargers that supplements product descriptions with technical charging data, translates them for four markets and uploads them directly back into the CMS. Without any external costs per AI token.

From enquiry to approach

## Where would you like to use AI?

It is not always clear where AI can add value, particularly if you do not build systems and workflows on a daily basis. AITJE brings AI and software engineering together to build a working solution for your needs. In doing so, we optimise the workflow, the choice of model and the costs.

See below how we help organisations and businesses move forward and find inspiration for your own work.

# Knowledge centre

Official page: https://aitje.com/en/knowledge

> Clear explanations of AI, models and your own AI environment. What is an LLM, what is local AI, what does an agent do? The AITJE knowledge centre.

AITJE is a Dutch AI specialist in local AI, automation and smarter workflows. Proprietary AI products, consultancy, development, installation and support, with independence as our guiding principle.

- [What is generative AI?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-generatieve-ai): Generative AI creates new content based on a prompt: text, images, music, video, 3D or code. What happens during the generation process, and how do you turn an interesting result into something useful for your work?
- [What is text generation using AI?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-tekstgeneratie): Text generation is the process of creating text using a language model. From draft emails and summaries to structured responses: the task and the available information determine the output.
- [What is image generation?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-image-generation): Image generation, or ‘beeldgeneratie’, enables AI to create new images or modify existing ones. A description or reference provides guidance; the model constructs the visual output.
- [What is music generation?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-music-generation): Music generation is the process of creating music using AI based on, for example, style, atmosphere, instruments or a sound clip. The model generates a musical composition which you can then listen to and edit.
- [What is speech and audio generation?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-spraak-en-audiogeneratie): With AI, you can convert text to speech and generate other sounds. How do text-to-speech, sound effects and transcription differ, and where do they fit into a practical workflow?
- [What is AI-powered video generation?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-videogeneratie): Video generation creates moving images from a description, an image or an existing clip. The model must not only produce attractive images, but also maintain continuity between successive frames.
- [What is 3D generation using AI?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-3d-generatie): 3D generation creates a digital spatial representation based on text or images. From concept object to textured model: the output is only usable when it is compatible with your design software and application.
- [What is code generation using AI?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-codegeneratie): Code generation allows a model to suggest, extend or adapt software code. The real value lies in the proposal fitting the existing project and being able to be implemented in a controlled manner.
- [How does generation work with diffusion models?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/hoe-werkt-generatie-met-diffusion-modellen): Many generative image models construct an image through successive steps starting from noise. What roles do the model, the prompt and the settings play during that process?
- [AI generation locally or via an API?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/ai-generatie-lokaal-of-via-een-api): Text, images and other output can sometimes be generated on your own hardware or produced via an external model service. Which approach best suits your data, desired quality and intended use?
- [What are frontier models?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-zijn-frontier-modellen): Frontier models are at the cutting edge of what AI is currently capable of. What does that say about quality, and when do you really need such a model?
- [What are open-source AI models?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-zijn-open-source-ai-modellen): Open source, open weights and free access do not mean the same thing. Find out what you can download, customise and run yourself — and what rights you need to do so.
- [What are tokens in AI?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-zijn-tokens): A language model works with tokens: small building blocks of input and output. They help determine how much context fits, how long a response takes and what an API request costs.
- [What is model routing?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-modelrouting): With model routing, a workflow selects which AI model will carry out a task. This allows you to combine local models and external APIs based on quality, data and costs.
- [What is quantisation in AI models?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-quantisatie): Quantisation stores model data with lower precision. As a result, a model may require less memory, but the impact on speed and quality varies depending on the application.
- [What is fine-tuning?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-fine-tuning): Fine-tuning further trains an existing model using targeted examples. When is this helpful, and when are a better prompt or document search function sufficient?
- [What is tool calling?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-tool-calling): With tool calling, a language model can suggest calling a function. Your software retrieves data or performs an action, within the permissions you set yourself.
- [What is MCP, the Model Context Protocol?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-mcp): MCP provides AI applications with a unified way of accessing tools and information sources. What does this make easier, and what do you still need to sort out yourself?
- [What are AI hallucinations?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-zijn-ai-hallucinaties): AI can provide a convincing answer that is factually incorrect. Learn how to recognise fabricated information and build applications that handle uncertainty more effectively.
- [What is digital sovereignty?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-digitale-soevereiniteit): Digital sovereignty is about having control over your data, systems and choices. In the context of AI, this also encompasses model access, management and the ability to switch providers.
- [What is ablation in language models?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-abliteration): Abliteration adjusts a model’s internal properties to reduce learned rejection behaviour. What does this change, and what does it not tell us about the quality?
- [What are the weights of an AI model?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-zijn-model-weights): Weights are the trained numbers that determine how a model processes information. Find out how model weights, parameters and a downloadable model file are related.
- [What is KV-cache in an LLM?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-kv-cache): The KV cache stores intermediate results from a language model, so that it does not have to repeat as much work during text generation. This helps with speed, but also requires memory.
- [What is a vector in AI?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-een-vector): A vector is an ordered sequence of numbers. In AI, such a sequence helps to represent, compare and retrieve information — for example, when searching by meaning.
- [What is a token factory?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-een-token-factory): A ‘token factory’ is a metaphor for infrastructure that produces AI output. What lies behind such a factory, and how does this relate to inference and costs?
- [What is inference in an LLM?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-inference): Inference is the process of using a trained model to produce an outcome. In the case of an LLM, this involves processing input and then constructing a response.
- [What is a vision model?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-een-vision-model): A vision model processes visual information, such as photographs and document images. A vision-language model combines this with language to answer questions about an image.
- [What is a coding model?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-een-coding-model): A coding model is designed for tasks involving software code. It can assist with explanations, additions and modifications, but a functioning development environment also requires tools and tests.
- [What is a VC subsidy for AI services?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-vc-subsidy): Investors and temporary grants can finance growth before a service pays for itself. How might such a potential grant affect your view of AI costs?
- [What is loss-leader pricing in the context of AI?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-loss-leader-pricing): With loss-leader pricing, an offer is priced at a loss to attract customers. How does this differ from a temporary discount, finance options and predatory pricing?
- [What is predatory pricing, or price gouging?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-predatory-pricing): Predatory pricing refers to low prices that can exclude competition. Why is a cheap AI API not in itself evidence of such a practice?
- [What is vendor lock-in in AI?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-vendor-lock-in): Vendor lock-in occurs when switching suppliers becomes difficult or expensive. With AI, this dependency often lies in data, APIs, model behaviour and workflows all at once.
- [What is an LLM?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-een-llm): An LLM is a large language model that can understand, predict and generate text. It often seems intelligent, but the quality of the result depends heavily on context, model choice and how you use it.
- [What is edge AI?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-edge-ai): Edge AI means that AI runs close to the source of the data, for example on a device, server or local network. This allows you to work faster and often gives you greater control over privacy, continuity and costs.
- [What is local AI?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-local-ai): Local AI means that AI runs within your own environment, for example on a local device, server or network. It is about having greater control over data, availability, costs and dependence on external AI platforms.
- [What is on-premises AI?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-on-premise-ai): On-premise AI means that AI runs on infrastructure managed by your own organisation or at your own premises. This can help with privacy, compliance, business continuity and control over systems.
- [White-label hardware, AITJE software](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/white-label-hardware-aitje-software): White-label hardware with ‘AITJE’ software means that ‘AITJE’ selects suitable hardware and provides the software layer, configuration and AI functionality tailored to the application.
- [What is RAG?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-rag): RAG is a method whereby a language model first retrieves relevant information from documents or a knowledge base before providing an answer. As a result, answers are often more specific, better substantiated and more useful for your own organisation.
- [What is context in AI?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-context): Context is all the additional information you provide to a model so that it better understands what you mean. Good context makes the difference between a generic answer and something that really suits your task, organisation or document.
- [What is a context window?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-een-context-window): The context window is the maximum amount of information a model can process in a single interaction. This determines how much text, chat history or document fragments can be used at any one time.
- [What is an AI agent?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-een-ai-agent): An AI agent is a system that not only provides answers, but can also take steps towards a goal. This includes retrieving information, making choices, using tools and carrying out a task partly automatically.
- [What are embeddings?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-zijn-embeddings): Embeddings convert text into vectors so that systems can recognise pieces of information that are similar in content. They form an important foundation for semantic search and many RAG applications.
- [What is prompt engineering?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-prompt-engineering): Prompt engineering is the deliberate formulation of instructions to ensure a model produces useful output. It is not about tricks, but about clarity regarding the objective, context, tone, preconditions and desired format.
- [What is an API?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-een-api): An API is an agreed method by which systems exchange data or functions with one another. It is the interface that allows software to communicate with other software without the need for manual copying and pasting.
- [What is a webhook?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-een-webhook): A webhook is an automatic message sent from one system to another as soon as something happens. This allows you to trigger processes immediately without having to constantly check for new information.
- [What is a backend?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-een-backend): The backend is the part of the software where processing, logic, integrations and data flows run behind the scenes, out of the user’s view. It is the technical layer that ensures an app or website can actually do something.
- [What is a front-end?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-een-frontend): The front end is the part of the software that users see and interact with directly. It encompasses screens, forms, feedback and interaction, and therefore relates to how user-friendly and intuitive a system is in practice.
- [What is the cloud?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-cloud): By ‘cloud’, organisations usually mean software, storage or computing power made available via external infrastructure. This offers flexibility, but also involves decisions regarding data, dependency and management.
- [What is a workflow?](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-een-workflow): A workflow is the fixed sequence of steps through which work, information and actions move through a process. Only once you have a clear understanding of your workflows can you truly assess where software, automation or AI adds value.

AITJE is a Dutch AI specialist in local AI, automation and smarter workflows. Proprietary AI products, consultancy, development, installation and support, with independence as our guiding principle.

AI is developing rapidly. Which models are suitable? What can you run on your own hardware? And how do you turn individual tools into something you can use on a daily basis?

AITJE explores the possibilities, builds what is needed and delivers a fully functional solution. From a specific consultancy request to a complete environment.

Our philosophy

## Control over what you use.

Knowing where your data is stored, what you’re paying for and who will help you if something goes wrong. For us, that’s part and parcel of a working AI solution.

Researching models, building software and integrating the components. From the initial experiment to a ready-to-use environment.

## Clients & implementation

Understanding the requirement, explaining the options and ensuring the solution fits into day-to-day work. With a focus on setup, explanation and the next steps.

# Frequently Asked Questions

Official page: https://aitje.com/en/faq

> Answers regarding AITJE, the AI products, services, collaboration, data and costs. Can’t find your question here? Discuss your AI enquiry with AITJE.

AITJE is a Dutch AI specialist in local AI, automation and smarter workflows. Proprietary AI products, consultancy, development, installation and support, with independence as our guiding principle.

## About AITJE

### What does AITJE do?

AITJE is a Dutch AI specialist with its own products. AITJE investigates where AI can make your work easier, better or cheaper, builds and installs the solution, and remains available afterwards. Often, that solution runs on your own hardware or server.

### Who is AITJE intended for?

For businesses, creators and professionals, as well as IT companies and agencies. This includes SMEs, local authorities, schools, the self-employed and developers. The sector is less important than the question: is there a specific problem that AI can help solve?

### Is AITJE opposed to cloud or external AI services?

No. The task determines the solution. AITJE prefers to operate locally or on its own server, but will use an external model where this is demonstrably more suitable. Dependency should be a conscious choice, not an unintended consequence.

### What sort of enquiries should you not direct to AITJE?

AITJE does not focus on medical systems, critical infrastructure or industrial engineering. However, an organisation in such a sector may still approach us for a specific application, such as administration or internal knowledge management.

### Who are the people behind AITJE?

Two founders and a permanent network of professionals who are called upon on a project-by-project basis. Read more [about AITJE](https://aitje.com/en/about-aitje).

## Services

### What is the difference between products, services and ‘AITJE Custom’?

Products are ready-to-use AI environments where AITJE has already done the legwork, such as AITJE Assistent and AITJE Coder. Services include research, consultancy, installation, optimisation and support. AITJE Custom offers bespoke AI: a solution built to meet your specific needs.

### Do I need to buy new hardware?

Not always. If your existing computer or server is suitable, AITJE can install the software on it. If additional processing power is required, AITJE will advise you on the best option. You can purchase it yourself or have it delivered via AITJE. Any hardware you pay for is yours to keep.

### Can I install a product myself?

Yes. You can order available products for self-installation on suitable hardware of your own.

### Which products are currently available?

AITJE Assistent AITJE Coder are currently in development. You can register your interest on their page.

### When will the other products become available?

No fixed date has been set yet. Let us know you’re interested on the product page, and you’ll be the first to hear. Need something similar right now? You might be able to arrange it via [AITJE Custom](https://aitje.com/en/services/aitje-custom).

## Products

### What is ‘AITJE Assistent’?

Your own AI chat assistant, similar to ChatGPT, but on your own device or server. You can write, summarise and ask questions, including about your own documents via the knowledge base.

### Does ‘AITJE Assistent’ work without an internet connection?

The local components do: chat, the knowledge base and management work as long as your device or server and the local network are available. Web search and updates require an internet connection.

### How much does AITJE Assistent cost?

The standalone product costs €499 per environment, with no per-user licence fee. Including basic installation, testing, training and agreed short-term aftercare, an introductory price of €599 applies; the standard price starts at €698. Introductory offer for Assistent and Coder for the first 100 paying customers. Availability will be confirmed in your quotation. Hardware, server hire and additional setup are quoted separately. All amounts are exclusive of VAT.

### Which file formats can I add to the knowledge base?

The knowledge base supports common file formats, such as PDF, CSV, Excel, TXT and Word (.docx). Do you have a different format? If so, we’ll work with you to determine the best way to import that information.

### Can AITJE Assistent also read scanned documents and images?

Yes. AITJE Assistent can also process information from scanned documents and images. How well this works depends, amongst other things, on the legibility and quality of the file.

### Can AITJE Assistent show which document an answer comes from?

Yes. For answers based on the knowledge base, the Assistant displays source references. This allows you to identify which documents were used and to compare the answer with the original information.

### What happens if documents in the knowledge base contradict one another?

The model indicates when the information found contradicts itself. In the knowledge manager, you can also assign a priority or weighting to categories or specific documents. This allows you to specify which sources should be given greater weight, for example, a current work instruction over an older document.

### How are amended or deleted documents processed in the knowledge base?

Changes are processed during database synchronisation. The information is broken down into searchable text segments, also known as chunks, and converted into vectors for the search index. During a chat, the Assistant retrieves the relevant information from this using RAG. The synchronisation ensures that changes and deletions are taken into account; prior to this processing, the previous version may still be present in the index.

### Can each department have its own secure knowledge base?

Yes. You can assign specific knowledge to particular user roles. This allows you to determine which employees have access to which information, for example by department or role.

### What is ‘AITJE Coder’?

A dedicated environment for coding agents: a local alternative to services such as Claude Code and Codex. Agents read and modify your code, execute commands and complete tasks iteratively.

### Does Coder work with my own tools?

Yes. Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Aider, Cline, Continue and other tools communicate with the box rather than with a cloud service. The /connect page on the box provides the certificate, your private key and a ready-to-use configuration for each tool. You enter tasks for the agent in the web app.

### How much does AITJE Coder cost?

The standalone product costs €699 per environment, with no per-user licence fee. Including basic installation, testing, training and agreed short-term aftercare, an introductory price of €799 applies; the standard price starts at €898. Introductory offer for Assistent and Coder for the first 100 paying customers. Availability will be confirmed in your quotation. Hardware, server hire and additional setup are quoted separately. All amounts are exclusive of VAT.

### Which programming languages and frameworks can AITJE Coder work with?

You can work with all programming languages and frameworks; Coder is not limited to a single fixed stack. You can provide additional documentation, instructions and project agreements via ‘skills’. The quality depends on the chosen model and the available context, so for a specific stack, we will test it against your tasks.

### Can AITJE Coder work on an existing codebase?

Yes. Coder can read, interpret and adapt existing projects. So you don’t need to start a new project. By providing project documentation and clear instructions, you give the agent context regarding the structure and conventions within your codebase.

### How do I determine which files and commands a coding agent is permitted to use?

For tasks carried out via the web app, the agent operates in a secure container with its own copy of the repository. It is permitted to install packages, but cannot access your internal network. You determine access on a per-repository basis; for GitHub, you log in once using a code, without having to create a token yourself. If you use your own tool, such as Claude Code or OpenCode, that tool determines which files and commands the agent is permitted to use.

### Can I review changes from AITJE Coder before they are applied?

Yes. For tasks carried out via the web app, nothing changes until you approve the result. You read the agent’s report and see every line that has been changed. Approving opens a pull request on GitHub, GitLab or Gitea; ‘Changes required’ rejects the request or has the agent start again. When using the tool interactively, your own tool determines when approval is required.

### Can ‘AITJE Coder’ also write tests and detect errors?

Yes. Coder can write tests, run existing tests and investigate errors. To do this, the agent can use your code, error messages and test results to suggest a change. You can then assess the tests and changes yourself.

## Services

### What is an AI-scan?

An analysis of up to three work processes, the systems you use and your current use of AI. Includes an initial consultation, approximately four hours of analysis, a concise report and a half-hour discussion. The introductory price is €395 for the first 10 paying customers; the standard price is €495. All prices are exclusive of VAT. The scope of the service and any travel or venue costs will be agreed in advance.

### What is token management and optimisation?

AITJE It maps out how your organisation uses AI and what that costs. It then examines subscriptions, model selection, agents and workflows, and makes adjustments where agreed. The aim is to reduce unnecessary usage whilst maintaining the required quality. Read more about [Token management & optimisation](https://aitje.com/en/services/token-management-en-optimalisatie).

### How does AITJE determine whether a cost saving comes at the expense of quality?

By testing the end result. ‘AITJE’ compares the original and the adapted workflow on the same tasks and assesses whether the outcome still meets the agreed requirements. Fewer tokens or a cheaper model only constitutes an improvement if the result remains good enough.

### Can we see how much AI usage costs for each workflow or department?

Yes, provided that usage is measurable and can be attributed. AITJE monitors subscriptions, model calls, token usage and other consumption per task or team. Where necessary, logging can be set up to gain that insight.

### What happens if a model API goes down or reaches its limit?

AITJE A fallback can be built: an alternative route or a different model that takes over the task. For critical steps, a local or edge model may be a good choice. Which fallback is possible depends on the task and is agreed upon during the setup.

### Can ‘AITJE’ prevent a stuck workflow from making endless API calls?

AITJE It can incorporate limits on attempts and costs, logging and clear stopping points. At key moments, an employee may first need to assess whether the workflow can continue: ‘human in the loop’. In this way, technical limits are combined with human oversight.

### What does ‘AITJE’ do under ‘Advice and Analysis’?

AITJE We develop your AI enquiry into concrete advice or a workable plan. This covers the technology, choice of model, costs, pitfalls, test cases and checks. You agree the level of detail and deliverables in advance.

### What does ‘Installation and setup’ cover?

A basic installation starts at €199 excluding VAT: installing the agreed software, testing it and providing guidance in a familiar, suitable environment, with brief follow-up support as agreed. We estimate this will take two to two and a half hours. Product costs, hardware or server hire, networking, comprehensive knowledge base setup and integrations are quoted separately.

### Can I use my AI environment securely from home or whilst on the move?

Yes. AITJE can set up remote access for you, with appropriate security and access rights. This feature is enabled separately and tailored to your network and the people who need to be able to use the environment.

### Can the same server run both AITJE Assistent and AITJE Coder?

AITJE Ideally, set up the Assistant and Coder in separate environments. This allows the capacity and configuration to be tailored to each product, and means they are less likely to interfere with one another when used simultaneously. A different architecture is possible if it suits your situation; the implications will be assessed in advance.

### How do I migrate my AI environment to different hardware?

A migration is preferably carried out in conjunction with ‘AITJE’, as a separate service. ‘AITJE’ helps you migrate the environment and export and transfer the vector database, text chunks and embeddings. Afterwards, checks are carried out to ensure that the knowledge base and the application are functioning correctly on the new hardware.

### Can AITJE improve my existing AI?

Yes. ‘AITJE’ examines how your current workflow, chatbot, knowledge search tool, voice agent or coding agent works. The improvement plan may cover instructions, skills, code, tool calling, the knowledge base, RAG or model selection. You choose which adjustments ‘AITJE’ carries out.

### How much does an AI data location check cost?

From €225 excluding VAT for a straightforward scenario, estimated at approximately three hours. We check a pre-agreed, limited number of known AI services, settings and available provider information. The basic assessment forms part of the AI scan. We reuse previous findings; additional technical research and measures are quoted separately.

### How does ‘AITJE’ help ensure the safe use of AI?

AITJE It maps out data flows, access, data locations and settings, and can implement practical measures. These include deleting personal data prior to an external model call, role-based access rights for the knowledge base, human verification, guardrails, usage limits and logging. The scope of the investigation and implementation is defined in advance.

### Can AITJE remove personal data before it is sent to an external model?

Yes. AITJE can incorporate a local preparatory step that removes or replaces names, contact details and other identifiable details, and forwards only the necessary information. Whether the result is truly anonymous also depends on the wider context. Replacing a name with a label does not automatically constitute full anonymisation.

### How can you prevent an employee from accessing restricted documents via AI?

The application verifies the identity and role before RAG retrieves data. The search query is restricted to authorised documents, text passages and categories. The same permissions apply to tool calls and other integrations. Restricted content should therefore not first be provided to the model with only the instruction not to share it.

### Can AI costs and the number of calls be limited?

Yes. AITJE can configure budgets, limits per task and user, rate limiting and a maximum number of attempts. Before a new call, the application can check whether there is still budget available. Provider warnings do not always result in an immediate halt; therefore, the system checks which limits actually cause a block. Ongoing calls and delayed usage reporting are taken into account in the configuration.

### How does AITJE Custom work?

AITJE Custom We can help with your questions and ideas regarding AI: automation, integrations, apps for mobile, desktop or tablet, AI agents and 3D/VR applications. We can also assist if you need help with existing code, workflows or prototypes. We investigate the appropriate combination of local and external AI, software and infrastructure, build and test the solution, and support the roll-out. We agree on the scope, hours and budget in advance for each phase.

### What does Support and Maintenance involve?

Core costs €49 per month for 30 minutes, Plus €129 for 1.5 hours and Max €249 for 3 hours, excluding VAT. Support, maintenance, personalised advice, checks, consultation and implementation are all included within that time budget. A general development update is separate from this. Additional work commences following your approval.

## Working together

### Where does a collaboration usually begin?

It starts with a discussion or demo, often followed by an [AI-scan](https://aitje.com/en/services/ai-scan). If you already have a specific enquiry, AITJE can also provide a proposal straight away.

### What does a demo involve?

A personalised online demonstration, for example via Google Meet. AITJE shows you what a product can do and discusses with you what suits your situation.

### Does AITJE collaborate with IT companies and agencies?

Yes. You manage the client relationship, whilst AITJE provides the AI expertise. You can agree on the level of AITJE’s visibility on a project-by-project basis. Read more at [For IT companies and agencies](https://aitje.com/en/services/voor-it-bedrijven).

### Can I call AITJE?

Please leave your telephone number via the [contact form](https://aitje.com/en/contact), or email contact@aitje.com.

## Data and in-house management

### Where is my data?

When used locally on your own hardware or server, documents and queries remain within your own environment. If you deliberately use a web search or an external model, the relevant information is sent to that service. AITJE clearly explains in advance what each function does.

### Is local AI always cheaper or safer?

Not automatically. Locally, you do not pay token costs, but you do pay for hardware, electricity and any maintenance. Whether it is more secure depends on the setup. AITJE will work through the options with you to find what suits your situation.

## Costs

### Where can I find the full price list?

[View the full price list (PDF)](https://aitje.com/pricelist-aitje.pdf) for all products, services, hourly rates and support subscriptions. You will also find details of what is included and the terms and conditions of the introductory offer. All amounts are exclusive of VAT.

### What are AITJE’s hourly rates?

AITJE charges €75 per hour, excluding VAT. You agree the work, estimated hours and budget in advance. Additional work only starts with your approval.

### How are the prices structured?

It consists of three components: the AI product or development, the hardware or server, and the installation. Support is optional and charged separately. All prices are exclusive of VAT.

### How does the introductory offer work?

The introductory offer for the first 10 paying customers applies to the AI-scan: €395 (regular price €495). For Assistent and Coder, the introductory offer for the first 100 paying customers applies: Assistent with basic installation €599 (regular price from €698) and Coder with basic installation €799 (regular price from €898). Availability will be confirmed in the quotation. Hardware, server hire, travel or venue costs and additional set-up will be quoted separately in advance. All amounts are exclusive of VAT.

### Do I have to pay again for research that has already been carried out during the scan?

We reuse findings from a scan or previous assignment. The basic assessment of AI usage, costs and data flows forms part of the scan. For follow-up work, you pay for additional analysis or implementation, with a scope and budget agreed in advance.

### What does ‘without external token costs’ mean?

With local use, you do not pay per query or per token to an external AI provider. You can use it as often as your hardware can handle. External models may, however, incur usage charges.

All products, services and hourly rates at a glance.

## Contact

[Contact AITJE](https://aitje.com/en/contact) — contact@aitje.com

# AITJE Assistent: Your own AI chat assistant. Under your control.

Official page: https://aitje.com/en/products/aitje-assistent

> AITJE Assistent: local chat with knowledge base. Stand-alone product €499; from €599 including basic installation. Excl. VAT and infrastructure.

Status: Available

AITJE Assistent is a dedicated ChatGPT-style environment for your entire team. Write, summarise, ask for explanations and base answers on your own documents: all within a single environment running on your own device or server.

Chat, local models, a [knowledge base](https://aitje.com/en/knowledge/wat-is-rag) and the management of accounts and roles are all included. If you need up-to-date information, you can deliberately enable web search from within the same environment.

## Who it is for

- Organisations wishing to have their own AI chat environment rather than individual subscriptions
- Offices dealing with sensitive or company-specific information, such as accountancy, legal practice or estate agency
- Teams that want to finally make internal manuals and documents searchable
- Schools and organisations wishing to manage users and access
- Creators and professionals who want their own assistant

## Capabilities

### Local chat

Write, summarise and ask for explanations using a model that runs on your own environment.

### Knowledge base

Add your own sources and base the answers on them.

### Accounts and roles

Determine who is authorised to do what, all from the same environment.

### Model selection

Choose the model for each task, with a reasoning mode for tricky questions.

### Web search if you wish

Make a point of using the online search function when you need up-to-date information.

### Works without an internet connection

The local infrastructure remains usable as long as your device or server and network are available.

## Included

- Chat environment with local models
- Knowledge base for your own resources, with a backup
- Accounts, roles and management
- Focus modes, model selection and reasoning mode
- Ongoing use of the delivered version, per environment or device

## Agreed separately

- Hardware or server costs
- Installation and setup by AITJE
- Cleaning up documents and setting up the knowledge base for you
- Updates, new models and post-delivery support
- External API or usage fees

### Without the internet

Chat with the installed model, ask questions about the local knowledge base, local documents and images, and manage settings. This requires your device or server and the local network to be available.

### With internet

Web searches, updates and new models, remote support where agreed, and external models if you specifically choose them.

### Capacity

Speed, model size, number of concurrent users and knowledge base capacity depend on the hardware or server. AITJE recommends a light or powerful environment based on your usage.

### System requirements

Minimum and recommended specifications will be confirmed prior to publication. Not sure whether your hardware is suitable? Ask AITJE.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is ‘AITJE Assistent’?

Your own AI chat assistant, similar to ChatGPT, but on your own device or server. You can write, summarise and ask questions, including about your own documents via the knowledge base.

### Does ‘AITJE Assistent’ work without an internet connection?

The local components do: chat, the knowledge base and management work as long as your device or server and the local network are available. Web search and updates require an internet connection.

### How much does AITJE Assistent cost?

The standalone product costs €499 per environment, with no per-user licence fee. Including basic installation, testing, training and agreed short-term aftercare, an introductory price of €599 applies; the standard price starts at €698. Introductory offer for Assistent and Coder for the first 100 paying customers. Availability will be confirmed in your quotation. Hardware, server hire and additional setup are quoted separately. All amounts are exclusive of VAT.

### How many people can use it at the same time?

There is no per-user licence. The practical number depends on the hardware or server and on how many people are working at the same time. AITJE advises on capacity based on your usage.

### Can you set up the knowledge base for me AITJE?

That’s possible. The knowledge base software is included with the product, and you can add sources yourself. AITJE can clean up and structure documents and set up focus modes as a separate assignment or as part of an SLA.

### Is AITJE Assistenta separate version?

No. It is a single product. How powerful your environment is depends on the hardware or server you choose.

### Which file formats can I add to the knowledge base?

The knowledge base supports common file formats, such as PDF, CSV, Excel, TXT and Word (.docx). Do you have a different format? If so, we’ll work with you to determine the best way to import that information.

### Can AITJE Assistent also read scanned documents and images?

Yes. AITJE Assistent can also process information from scanned documents and images. How well this works depends, amongst other things, on the legibility and quality of the file.

### Can AITJE Assistent show which document an answer comes from?

Yes. For answers based on the knowledge base, the Assistant displays source references. This allows you to identify which documents were used and to compare the answer with the original information.

### What happens if documents in the knowledge base contradict one another?

The model indicates when the information found contradicts itself. In the knowledge manager, you can also assign a priority or weighting to categories or specific documents. This allows you to specify which sources should be given greater weight, for example, a current work instruction over an older document.

### How are amended or deleted documents processed in the knowledge base?

Changes are processed during database synchronisation. The information is broken down into searchable text segments, also known as chunks, and converted into vectors for the search index. During a chat, the Assistant retrieves the relevant information from this using RAG. The synchronisation ensures that changes and deletions are taken into account; prior to this processing, the previous version may still be present in the index.

### Can each department have its own secure knowledge base?

Yes. You can assign specific knowledge to particular user roles. This allows you to determine which employees have access to which information, for example by department or role.

# AITJE Coder: Your own coding agents. With no external token costs.

Official page: https://aitje.com/en/products/aitje-coder

> AITJE Coder: your own local coding agents. Stand-alone product €699; from €799 including basic installation. Excluding VAT and infrastructure.

Status: Available

AITJE Coder is a proprietary alternative to services such as Codex and Claude Code: a complete local coding environment that reads and modifies projects, executes commands and completes programming tasks iteratively.

AITJE has already done the legwork. Selected local coding models, an agent with review and pull requests, a web app for management and integration with tools such as Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex and Aider are all included, ready to use, in a single product.

## Who it is for

- Development agencies that work with coding agents on a daily basis
- Companies with their own development team
- Freelance developers and technical creators
- Professionals who wish to use their own or spare hardware
- Teams seeking greater control over models, infrastructure and costs

## Capabilities

### Terminal and CLI

Work from your own terminal with models running locally.

### AITJE-interface

A graphical interface for those who prefer not to work in the terminal.

### Supported harnesses

Connect Coder to Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Aider and other coding agents.

### Selected models

Light, fast or powerful: you choose according to the task, without needing to know the model names.

### Iterative working

Agents read and modify projects, execute commands and complete tasks.

### Works without an internet connection

The local core remains usable without a connection to an external model provider.

## Included

- Selected local coding models, configured for the box
- Agent with live progress tracking, reviews and pull requests to GitHub, GitLab or Gitea
- Graphical user AITJE, API access and CLI
- Integration with Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Aider and other tools
- Ongoing use of the delivered version, per environment or device

## Agreed separately

- Hardware or server costs
- Installation and setup by AITJE
- Organisation- or project-specific workflows and integrations
- Updates, new models and post-delivery support
- External API or usage fees

### Without the internet

Working with the installed models, programming via GUI, API, CLI and locally available frameworks, and reading, modifying and executing local projects.

### With internet

Searching for online documentation, downloading new models, using packages and Git services, and remote support where agreed.

### Capacity

Speed, model variant, context capacity and the number of concurrent users depend on the hardware. A larger team may require a server or more than one environment.

### Compatibility

Configurations are available for Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex CLI, Aider, Cline, Roo Code, Kilo Code, Continue and Zed. Claude Code communicates directly with the box’s Anthropic Messages API, whilst the other tools use an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Coder does not guarantee compatibility with every tool.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is ‘AITJE Coder’?

A dedicated environment for coding agents: a local alternative to services such as Claude Code and Codex. Agents read and modify your code, execute commands and complete tasks iteratively.

### Does Coder work with my own tools?

Yes. Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Aider, Cline, Continue and other tools communicate with the box rather than with a cloud service. The /connect page on the box provides the certificate, your private key and a ready-to-use configuration for each tool. You enter tasks for the agent in the web app.

### How much does AITJE Coder cost?

The standalone product costs €699 per environment, with no per-user licence fee. Including basic installation, testing, training and agreed short-term aftercare, an introductory price of €799 applies; the standard price starts at €898. Introductory offer for Assistent and Coder for the first 100 paying customers. Availability will be confirmed in your quotation. Hardware, server hire and additional setup are quoted separately. All amounts are exclusive of VAT.

### Are local models good enough for real-world applications?

For many tasks, certainly – especially if you keep them simple and clear. See how a marketing agency uses AITJE Coder [25 to create new game levels every week](https://aitje.com/en/cases/coder-game-in-24-uur), or request a demo to discuss the possibilities for your own work.

### Can I add another model myself?

Yes. Adding or removing a local model is done on the box itself; AITJE can do this for you either as a standalone service or via an SLA. An administrator can also add an external provider. By default, these models are not accessible to anyone: you grant access to them on a per-user basis.

### Which programming languages and frameworks can AITJE Coder work with?

You can work with all programming languages and frameworks; Coder is not limited to a single fixed stack. You can provide additional documentation, instructions and project agreements via ‘skills’. The quality depends on the chosen model and the available context, so for a specific stack, we will test it against your tasks.

### Can AITJE Coder work on an existing codebase?

Yes. Coder can read, interpret and adapt existing projects. So you don’t need to start a new project. By providing project documentation and clear instructions, you give the agent context regarding the structure and conventions within your codebase.

### How do I determine which files and commands a coding agent is permitted to use?

For tasks carried out via the web app, the agent operates in a secure container with its own copy of the repository. It is permitted to install packages, but cannot access your internal network. You determine access on a per-repository basis; for GitHub, you log in once using a code, without having to create a token yourself. If you use your own tool, such as Claude Code or OpenCode, that tool determines which files and commands the agent is permitted to use.

### Can I review changes from AITJE Coder before they are applied?

Yes. For tasks carried out via the web app, nothing changes until you approve the result. You read the agent’s report and see every line that has been changed. Approving opens a pull request on GitHub, GitLab or Gitea; ‘Changes required’ rejects the request or has the agent start again. When using the tool interactively, your own tool determines when approval is required.

### Can ‘AITJE Coder’ also write tests and detect errors?

Yes. Coder can write tests, run existing tests and investigate errors. To do this, the agent can use your code, error messages and test results to suggest a change. You can then assess the tests and changes yourself.

# AI-scan: Where can AI improve your work?

Official page: https://aitje.com/en/services/ai-scan

> AITJE’s AI-scan: approximately four hours of analysis covering up to three processes, a concise report and a discussion. Introductory price: €395, excluding VAT.

The AI-scan examines up to three key work processes. AITJE looks at tasks, systems, information and current AI usage to determine where time, money or quality is being lost. During the intake, we work with you to select the processes and staff involved.

You will receive a practical report setting out specific opportunities and priorities. This will enable you to decide what you wish to improve and what is required to do so. The outcome may also be that you do not need to make any changes for the time being.

## Who it is for

- Companies wishing to discover what AI can do for their business
- Organisations that already use AI but lack an overview
- Anyone unsure whether their current subscriptions and models are a good fit
- Anyone wishing to use AI more securely, more cost-effectively or more independently

## The approach

### Brief intake

Why do you want the scan, which people and processes are relevant, and will the scan take place on-site or remotely?

### Half-day research session

Approximately four hours of interviews and process analysis: who does what, using which systems, and where do delays or duplication of work occur?

### Targeted monitoring

With your consent, AITJE will carry out limited reviews of software, examples or workflows where necessary.

### Report

A concise, practical report setting out opportunities, priorities, risks and next steps. You will then discuss the results in a meeting lasting approximately half an hour.

## Deliverables

- Overview of the processes analysed and your current use of AI
- Basic assessment of AI subscriptions, costs and data flows
- Specific opportunities to implement or improve AI
- A practical prioritisation of those opportunities
- The expected impact on work, quality, costs or continuity
- Risks, points to note and recommended next steps
- Where reasonably possible: a rough estimate of costs or savings
- A discussion of the report and the recommended next steps

## Prices and conditions

€395. All prices exclude VAT.

Introductory offer for the AI-scan for the first 10 paying customers. Availability will be confirmed in your quotation. Standard price: €495. Includes an intake, approximately four hours’ analysis of up to three processes, an assessment, a concise report and a half-hour discussion. The scope and any travel or venue costs will be agreed in advance.

Introductory offer for the AI-scan for the first 10 paying customers. Availability will be confirmed in your quotation.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is an AI-scan?

An analysis of up to three work processes, the systems you use and your current use of AI. Includes an initial consultation, approximately four hours of analysis, a concise report and a half-hour discussion. The introductory price is €395 for the first 10 paying customers; the standard price is €495. All prices are exclusive of VAT. The scope of the service and any travel or venue costs will be agreed in advance.

### Should AITJE come round?

Not necessarily. The scan can be carried out on-site or remotely, depending on what is necessary and practical.

### Is the scan also useful if my company does not yet use AI?

Yes. Your existing work is the starting point. ‘AITJE’ examines where information searches, repetitive actions or other tasks could potentially be improved. You do not yet need to have chosen a model, application or AI plan.

### What do I need to prepare?

During the intake, you’ll discuss which processes and staff members are relevant. Specific examples of the work, the software used and any AI subscriptions will help us understand the situation. Together with AITJE, you’ll decide what information is required for this and what may be shared.

### Does the AI-scan also look at subscriptions and token costs?

### Am I then committed to a follow-up assignment?

No. The report is yours, even if you do not subsequently purchase anything from AITJE. The outcome may even be that you do not need to make any changes for the time being.

# Token management & optimisation: The right AI for every step. Lower costs per result.

Official page: https://aitje.com/en/services/token-management-en-optimalisatie

> AITJE Maps out AI usage and costs for content, knowledge, images and code. Optimise subscriptions, models and workflows. Available as a standalone service or as a follow-up to the AI scan.

Where are your AI budget and tokens going? ‘AITJE’ identifies which teams are using AI, for which tasks, and via which subscriptions, APIs and in-house models. From writing text and searching for knowledge to generating images, building code and other applications.

AITJE then investigates which setup is most suitable: multiple smaller subscriptions, a shared model budget, groups of specialised agents, or a combination of external, local and edge models. The choice is based on the workload, quality and total cost per usable result.

The workflow itself is also important. Dividing tasks, providing specific information and carrying out fixed actions using code can reduce unnecessary token usage. This service can be purchased separately; the [AI-scan](https://aitje.com/en/services/ai-scan) provides a broad overview of your usage and opportunities for optimisation.

## Who it is for

- Teams with individual AI subscriptions and little overview
- Organisations with high or fluctuating API costs
- Those who use AI for content, knowledge, images or code
- Companies with agents and automated workflows
- Anyone wishing to combine external, local and edge models
- IT companies that manage the use of AI for clients

## The approach

### Usage guide

Which teams use AI, for which tasks and at what cost? ‘AITJE’ identifies subscriptions, models, tokens and other usage, such as image credits. Where available, quality, turnaround time and repetitive work are also measured.

### Choosing the setup

Based on your requirements, AITJE compares subscriptions, APIs and suitable external, local and edge models. Shared budgets and groups of specialist agents may also form part of the approach.

### Tailor as appropriate

Within the agreed scope, tasks are allocated, prompts are refined and data is retrieved in a targeted manner. Code handles the routine work; the chosen model is provided with the correct context. Where useful, limits, the reuse of results and central model routing are incorporated.

### Checking the result

AITJE It compares the costs, quality and speed before and after the adjustments, including any additional attempts. Documentation, logging and agreed management help to monitor usage going forward.

## Deliverables

- Overview of AI usage by team and task, where measurable
- Insight into subscriptions, tokens, API costs and other model usage
- A well-founded proposal for models, budgets and workflows
- The agreed changes to model calls, context and task allocation
- A comparison of costs and quality before and after implementation
- Logging and usage limits as agreed
- Documentation and agreements regarding data, access and, where applicable, management

## Prices and conditions

Fixed hourly rate. All prices exclude VAT.

An hourly estimate is provided in advance for assessment, comparison, implementation and, where applicable, management. You can also opt to have just an analysis carried out. We reuse findings from the AI scan. Subscriptions, model usage, hardware and hosting are quoted separately.

## Agreed separately

- External API costs, hardware, hosting or software licences
- A fixed saving or the same outcome for every workflow
- Ongoing management outside the agreed scope of the assignment

## Frequently asked questions

### What is token management and optimisation?

AITJE It maps out how your organisation uses AI and what that costs. It then examines subscriptions, model selection, agents and workflows, and makes adjustments where agreed. The aim is to reduce unnecessary usage whilst maintaining the required quality. Read more about [Token management & optimisation](https://aitje.com/en/services/token-management-en-optimalisatie).

### Is this part of the AI-scan or a separate service?

Both. The [AI-scan](https://aitje.com/en/services/ai-scan) provides a broad overview of your current AI usage, subscriptions and opportunities for optimisation. A comprehensive model comparison, workflow adjustments and ongoing management are covered under a separately agreed engagement. You can also purchase this service directly, without first carrying out a scan.

### Is it just about language models and APIs?

No. ‘AITJE’ also considers AI usage via subscriptions and applications for content, knowledge, images, code and other tasks. Not every service is billed in tokens: for images, audio or video, for example, credits, the number of images or minutes may be relevant. This usage data is factored into the cost per usable result.

### Could a different combination of subscriptions be more cost-effective?

That’s possible. Multiple smaller subscriptions, a shared model budget or API usage may be a better fit than the current setup. AITJE compares actual usage, included capacity, limits, quality and terms and conditions. Which combination is right depends on your team and tasks.

### What does AITJE mean by ‘agent clusters’?

Groups of agents, each carrying out a specific part of the work, such as retrieving information, writing text and checking the result. Each step can be assigned a suitable model and specific context. AITJE assesses whether this division of labour adds value to your workflow; additional agents may also mean extra calls and management overhead.

### Does this work with frontier, local and edge models?

Yes. AITJE can combine advanced models via external APIs with models on its own servers or local devices. Edge models run on, or close to, the device where the task takes place. The task, capacity and data flows determine the most suitable approach. With in-house models, hardware, power, hosting and management remain part of the costs.

### Does AITJE always choose the cheapest model?

No. ‘AITJE’ tests your tasks and compares quality, speed, usage and the number of attempts. A model with a lower token price may require more calls; a more expensive model may actually work out cheaper for a particular step.

### Can a workflow be set up to send results from €4 to €0.40?

This is a sample calculation, not a firm commitment. Assuming a hypothetical flat rate of €4 per million tokens, one million tokens would cost €4 and one hundred thousand tokens would cost €0.40. The achievable savings depend on the workflow, output, quality and retries. Costs for code, hosting, management and development are separate from this.

### What does the code do instead of the LLM?

For example, retrieving data via an API, selecting relevant fields, performing calculations and checking the output against fixed rules. The model is given a clearly defined task with specific context, rather than all the raw data and steps in a single large prompt.

### Can AITJE also build new workflows and manage API calls?

Yes. AITJE can build a central layer for model calls and a new workflow, including routing, logging, budgets and limits. Access, key management and a form of ongoing management are also agreed in advance.

### What is the difference between this and optimisation?

This service focuses on AI usage and costs within your organisation: subscriptions, models, agents and workflows. [Optimisation](https://aitje.com/en/services/optimalisatie) assesses an existing AI solution more broadly, for example in terms of reliability, stability and human oversight.

### How does AITJE determine whether a cost saving comes at the expense of quality?

By testing the end result. ‘AITJE’ compares the original and the adapted workflow on the same tasks and assesses whether the outcome still meets the agreed requirements. Fewer tokens or a cheaper model only constitutes an improvement if the result remains good enough.

### Can we see how much AI usage costs for each workflow or department?

Yes, provided that usage is measurable and can be attributed. AITJE monitors subscriptions, model calls, token usage and other consumption per task or team. Where necessary, logging can be set up to gain that insight.

### What happens if a model API goes down or reaches its limit?

AITJE A fallback can be built: an alternative route or a different model that takes over the task. For critical steps, a local or edge model may be a good choice. Which fallback is possible depends on the task and is agreed upon during the setup.

### Can ‘AITJE’ prevent a stuck workflow from making endless API calls?

AITJE It can incorporate limits on attempts and costs, logging and clear stopping points. At key moments, an employee may first need to assess whether the workflow can continue: ‘human in the loop’. In this way, technical limits are combined with human oversight.

[Contact AITJE](https://aitje.com/en/contact) — contact@aitje.com

### What does ‘Installation and setup’ cover?

A basic installation starts at €199 excluding VAT: installing the agreed software, testing it and providing guidance in a familiar, suitable environment, with brief follow-up support as agreed. We estimate this will take two to two and a half hours. Product costs, hardware or server hire, networking, comprehensive knowledge base setup and integrations are quoted separately.

### Do I need to buy new hardware?

No. AITJE first assesses whether your existing hardware is suitable for the chosen models, the memory requirements and the expected usage. You can also purchase hardware yourself based on their advice. If a new environment is required, AITJE can help you find and arrange it.

### Can I choose my own server or hosting provider?

Yes. You can choose your own server or arrange the hosting yourself, after which AITJE will carry out the agreed installation. A check is carried out in advance to ensure that the capacity, operating system, access and network are compatible with the solution. ### What hardware and server environments does AITJE use?

AITJE It works with, amongst others, BOSGAME M5 and M6 and Mac mini, and for more demanding applications with, for example, NVIDIA DGX Spark or Dell PowerEdge. A droplet, VPS or GPU-VPS, for example at Nebius, may also be suitable. These are options, not fixed hardware requirements: the application, models and required capacity determine the choice.

### What do I need to provide before installation?

This will be agreed in advance. This includes information about previously purchased hardware, server access, network settings and the documents the solution needs to use, such as training materials or internal manuals. ### Can this be done remotely?

Often, yes. A server can usually be set up entirely remotely. An on-site visit is usually necessary if physical hardware needs to be connected.

### Can I use my AI environment securely from home or whilst on the move?

Yes. AITJE can set up remote access for you, with appropriate security and access rights. This feature is enabled separately and tailored to your network and the people who need to be able to use the environment.

### Can the same server run both AITJE Assistent and AITJE Coder?

AITJE Ideally, set up the Assistant and Coder in separate environments. This allows the capacity and configuration to be tailored to each product, and means they are less likely to interfere with one another when used simultaneously. A different architecture is possible if it suits your situation; the implications will be assessed in advance.

### How do I migrate my AI environment to different hardware?

A migration is preferably carried out in conjunction with ‘AITJE’, as a separate service. ‘AITJE’ helps you migrate the environment and export and transfer the vector database, text chunks and embeddings. Afterwards, checks are carried out to ensure that the knowledge base and the application are functioning correctly on the new hardware.
